title: Mesenteric adipose-derived exosomal TINAGL1 enhances intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's Disease via SMAD4.
authors: Chen, Yidong; Li, Junrong; Zhang, Xiaopeng; Li, Shuang; Cheng, Yiyu; Fu, Xiaoyu; Li, Jiamin; Zhu, Liangru
one_liner_zh: 该文研究克罗恩病肠纤维化中脂肪外泌体TINAGL1与SMAD4的蛋白互作，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白对接而非TF-DNA互作，且方法以实验为主，仅少量蛋白对接，与课题核心关联较弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Crohn's Disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory condition characterized by intestinal fibrosis, severely impacting patient quality of life. The molecular mechanisms driving this fibrosis remain inadequately understood. Recent evidence implicates mesenteric adipose tissue (MAT) in CD pathogenesis, particularly through its exosome secretion, which may influence fibrogenic pathways. Understanding the role of MAT-derived exosomes is crucial for unraveling these molecular processes. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to elucidate the role of MAT-derived exosomes in CD-related intestinal fibrosis. We focus on investigating their molecular composition and the potential impact on fibrosis progression, with an emphasis on identifying novel therapeutic targets. METHODS: We induced chronic intestinal inflammation in mice using dinitrobenzene sulfonic acid (DNBS), simulating CD-like fibrosis. Exosomes were isolated from DNBS-treated mice (MG) and normal controls (NG) for characterization using electron microscopy and proteomic analysis. Additionally, human colonic fibroblasts were exposed to exosomes from CD patients and healthy individuals, with subsequent assessment of fibrogenesis through proteomic and RNA sequencing analyses. RESULTS: Proteomic analyses revealed a significant activation of the TGF-beta signaling pathway in MG-treated mice compared to controls, correlating with enhanced intestinal fibrosis. In vitro experiments demonstrated that colonic fibroblasts exposed to CD patient-derived exosomes exhibited increased fibrogenic activity. Protein docking and co-immunoprecipitation studies suggested a critical interaction between TINAGL1 and SMAD4, enhancing fibrosis. Importantly, in vivo experiments corroborated that recombinant TINAGL1 protein exacerbated DNBS-induced intestinal fibrosis. CONCLUSION: Our findings highlight the pivotal role of MAT-derived exosomes, particularly those carrying TINAGL1, in the progression of intestinal fibrosis in CD. The involvement of the TGF-beta signaling pathway, especially the SMAD4 protein, offers new insights into the molecular mechanisms of CD-related fibrosis and presents potential targets for therapeutic intervention.
abstract_zh: 引言：克罗恩病（Crohn's Disease, CD）是一种以肠道纤维化为特征的慢性炎症性疾病，严重影响患者生活质量。驱动该纤维化的分子机制仍未被充分理解。近期证据表明，肠系膜脂肪组织（mesenteric adipose tissue, MAT）在CD发病机制中发挥作用，尤其是通过其外泌体分泌，可能影响纤维化通路。理解MAT来源外泌体的作用对于揭示这些分子过程至关重要。目的：本研究旨在阐明MAT来源外泌体在CD相关肠道纤维化中的作用。我们重点研究其分子组成及对纤维化进展的潜在影响，并强调识别新型治疗靶点。方法：我们使用二硝基苯磺酸（dinitrobenzene sulfonic acid, DNBS）诱导小鼠慢性肠道炎症，模拟CD样纤维化。从DNBS处理小鼠（MG）和正常对照（NG）中分离外泌体，通过电子显微镜和蛋白质组学分析进行表征。此外，将人结肠成纤维细胞暴露于CD患者和健康个体的外泌体，随后通过蛋白质组学和RNA测序分析评估纤维化生成。结果：蛋白质组学分析显示，与对照组相比，MG处理小鼠中TGF-beta信号通路显著激活，与肠道纤维化增强相关。体外实验表明，暴露于CD患者来源外泌体的结肠成纤维细胞表现出增加的纤维化活性。蛋白质对接和共免疫沉淀研究提示TINAGL1与SMAD4之间的关键相互作用，增强纤维化。重要的是，体内实验证实重组TINAGL1蛋白加剧了DNBS诱导的肠道纤维化。结论：我们的发现强调了MAT来源外泌体，特别是携带TINAGL1的外泌体，在CD肠道纤维化进展中的关键作用。TGF-beta信号通路，尤其是SMAD4蛋白的参与，为CD相关纤维化的分子机制提供了新见解，并呈现了治疗干预的潜在靶点。
